Directors agreed on neutral fiscal stance, recommended targeted support vs untargeted fuel subsidies, urged supply-side reforms for corruption/crime/rule of law. Broadly supported financial stability framework. Relevant to 5B.3 (fiscal rules), 5B.4 (competition/rule of law), 5B.5 (anticorruption), 5B.9 (inflation), 5B.10 (growth).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0004","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0003","unit-0005"],"explanation":"Selected Economic Indicators table for 2021-2023. Contains GDP growth, unemployment, inflation, fiscal balance, debt, monetary and external sector data. Weak relevance as tabular data but provides baseline for 5B.8 (employment), 5B.9 (inflation), 5B.10 (growth trajectory).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0005","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.9","5B.10","5B.1","5B.3"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0004","unit-0006"],"explanation":"Key Issues context. Discusses slower pandemic recovery than peers, inflation acceleration, tightened financial conditions, weakened U.S. growth prospects. Identifies long-standing problems of low growth and high inequality. Lists main policy recommendations including fiscal policy (market-based fuel pricing, targeted support), monetary policy (restrictive rate), financial sector policies, structural policies for growth. Relevant to 5B.9 (inflation shock), 5B.10 (growth trajectory), 5B.1 (fiscal agenda), 5B.3 (monetary framework).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0006","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0005","unit-0007"],"explanation":"Mission team composition and approved by information. Lists officials met (Finance Secretary, Banxico Governor, Labor Secretary, Economy Secretary). Contains Table of Contents listing sections on context, recent developments, outlook/risks, policy discussions on inflation, downside risks, financial system, growth. No substantive policy content relevant to Chapter 5B questions.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0008","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.10","5B.4","5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0007","unit-0009"],"explanation":"CONTEXT section. Mexico facing challenging environment as global inflation surged. Economy recovered more gradually than peers. Identifies long-standing problems of low growth, weak productivity, high inequality. Notes obstacles to higher growth: rule of law, corruption, crime issues, regional disparities, weak education/health outcomes. Relevant to 5B.10 (growth trajectory), 5B.4 (competition/rule of law), 5B.5 (corruption).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0009","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.9","5B.10","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0008","unit-0010"],"explanation":"RECENT DEVELOPMENTS. Economic recovery picked up pace in H1 2022 with GDP expansion of 1.8%. Labor market improved ahead of output. Headline inflation rose from 3% (end-2020) to 7.4% (end-2021) to 8.7% (August 2022). Energy price inflation moderated due to fuel subsidies. Food inflation rose to 14.1%. Core inflation at 8.1%. Relevant to 5B.9 (inflation shocks), 5B.10 (growth recovery), 5B.8 (labor market distribution).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0010","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.8","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0009","unit-0011"],"explanation":"Continued Recent Developments. Capacity utilization data for manufacturing. Unemployment and underemployment rates. Sector-specific recovery showing goods-producing and some services above pre-pandemic levels while construction remained below. Relevant to 5B.8 (employment distribution across sectors), 5B.10 (differentiated sector recovery).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0011","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0010","unit-0012"],"explanation":"Financial conditions tightened. Banxico responded with acceleration in monetary tightening from 25bp initial hikes to 50bp and 75bp hikes as inflation became broad-based. Policy rate at 9.25%, about 6pp above U.S. Fed. Interest rates and bond yields at highest since Global Financial Crisis. Real yield on inflation-linked Udibonos rose 80bps. Relevant to 5B.3 (monetary policy response), 5B.9 (inflation shock management).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0012","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0011","unit-0013"],"explanation":"Credit growth recovering despite tighter conditions. Bank credit to non-financial corporates picking up. Mexican banking system remains well-capitalized with profitability recovering. Total capital adequacy ratio increased to over 19% from 16% pre-pandemic. Large institutions maintain ample liquidity buffers. Relevant to 5B.3 (financial system stability), 5B.5 (banking supervision).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0013","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0012","unit-0014"],"explanation":"PEMEX benefited from higher global oil prices. Earnings doubled to USD 23 billion in H1 2022. Improved cash generation allowed rise in capital expenditures but mostly used for debt amortization. Total debt remains high including to suppliers. Spreads on external debt above government bonds and oil sector peers. Weak relevance to 5B.3 (state enterprise governance), 5B.10 (economic trajectory).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0014","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.9","5B.10","5B.3"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0013","unit-0015"],"explanation":"OUTLOOK AND RISKS. Economic activity expected to slow in H2 2022 and 2023 given tighter global financial conditions and cooling U.S. growth. Projected growth 2.1% (2022) and 1.2% (2023). Inflation projected to plateau at 8.5% then gradually decline. Balance of risks tilted to downside including higher domestic/global inflation, sharper tightening, sharper U.S. slowdown. Detailed risk assessment including commodity price shocks, capital outflow risks, domestic inflation persistence. Pivotal for 5B.9 (shock management) and 5B.10 (growth trajectory).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0015","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.9","5B.10","5B.3"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0014","unit-0016"],"explanation":"Authorities' Views on outlook. Budget contemplates 2023 growth in range 1.2-3.0% (central 2.1%). Latest Banxico forecast 0.8-2.4% (central 1.6%). Authorities see inflation falling in 2023 under normalization of supply shocks, fiscal measures for fuel prices, decisive monetary policy. See U.S. slowdown as headline risk. Note manufacturing might be less affected than services. Expect benefit from nearshoring. Relevant to 5B.9 (shock response), 5B.10 (growth trajectory), 5B.3 (policy coordination).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0016","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.9","5B.3","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0015","unit-0017"],"explanation":"Box 2: Global Tightening and Inflation Scenario. Multi-layer shock simulation: (1) Oil/food price shock (10%/50% rise), (2) inflation expectations dislocation causing sharper rate increases, (3) 1% domestic demand decline. Results: peak output loss exceeding 2% below baseline, elevated systemic liquidity risk. Pivotal for 5B.9 (shock management) and 5B.3 (monetary response to inflation).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0017","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0016","unit-0018"],"explanation":"POLICY DISCUSSIONS A. Tackling High Inflation - Monetary Policy. Banxico proactive approach to address broad-based inflation. Since June 2021, gradually larger rate increases brought ex ante real policy rate to moderately restrictive level (~4%) by September 2022. Appropriately calibrated response to upward inflation surprises. Policy rate of at least 10% expected to return inflation to 3% target within two years. Pivotal for 5B.3 (monetary policy credibility) and 5B.9 (inflation management).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0018","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0017","unit-0019"],"explanation":"Continued monetary policy discussion. Inflation risks expected to remain heightened. Uncertainty about timing/speed/durability of downward inflation path. Sources of uncertainty: further shocks from commodity prices, imported inflation persistence, supply chain constraints, minimum wage increases feeding into costs, domestic price adjustment inertia, upticks in near-term expectations. Shows real ex-ante policy rates comparison with Brazil, Chile, Peru, Colombia. Pivotal for 5B.3 and 5B.9.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0019","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0018","unit-0020"],"explanation":"Risk considerations call for further policy rate increases and maintaining restrictive stance. Risks to inflation are not only high but asymmetric - upside surprises more likely than downside. Philips curve estimates show backward-looking elements in Mexico's inflation process. Risk management approach argues for real ex-ante rate peaking at over 5% in 2023. Pivotal for 5B.3 (monetary policy credibility) and 5B.9 (inflation shock management).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0020","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9","5B.7"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0019","unit-0021"],"explanation":"Clear monetary policy communication emphasized. Banxico publishing updated inflation forecasts with every rate decision since August 2021. Guidance on direction of next policy rate change in statements. Recommendation to publish more information on policy rate path underlying macro forecast. Broader review of inflation targeting framework experience suggested for improvements. Relevant to 5B.3 (policy communication), 5B.7 (reliable economic information), 5B.9 (inflation expectations).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0021","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.9","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0020","unit-0022"],"explanation":"Fiscal Measures. Authorities used largely untargeted subsidies to mitigate cost of living rise. Subsidies expected to cost around 2% of GDP including: retail fuel price stabilization (estimated 1.5% GDP budgetary cost, reduced inflation by ~2pp but disproportionately benefited higher income households), measures for food prices (smaller budgetary cost, minimal direct inflation impact). Relevant to 5B.1 (fiscal agenda - rents/loyalty), 5B.9 (shock mitigation), 5B.8 (distribution of gains/burdens).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0022","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.8","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0021","unit-0023"],"explanation":"Continued fiscal measures. Fiscal and redistributive measures helped support real incomes. Deficit increased only ~0.25% GDP with fuel subsidies offset by higher oil revenues. Increased universal social pensions, minimum wage projected to rise from 42% to 59% of median formal sector wage (2018-2022). Real per capita labor income increased ~5% y/y by mid-2022. Relevant to 5B.1 (fiscal priorities), 5B.8 (wage distribution), 5B.9 (shock mitigation).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0023","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0022","unit-0024"],"explanation":"Proposed neutral fiscal stance in 2023 strikes balance between supporting monetary policy in disinflation while avoiding material fiscal drag. With economy operating close to potential, priority is restoring low/stable inflation. Restrictive monetary + neutral fiscal is appropriate mix. Note continuing large minimum wage increases will likely add inflation pressures, potentially reducing formal employment for lower income workers. Relevant to 5B.1 (policy coordination), 5B.3 (fiscal/monetary mix), 5B.9 (inflation management).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0024","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.1","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0023","unit-0025"],"explanation":"Authorities' Views on monetary and anti-inflationary fiscal measures. Authorities agreed robust monetary policy needed to keep inflation expectations anchored. Highlighted strengthened communication ensuring smooth financial market adjustment. Anti-inflationary fiscal measures mitigated effects on most exposed. Fuel price stabilization central to supporting households and restraining inflation. Relevant to 5B.3 (monetary credibility), 5B.1 (fiscal policy), 5B.9 (shock response).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0025","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.9","5B.3"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0024","unit-0026"],"explanation":"B. Managing Potential Downside Risks - Fiscal Policy. Fiscal policy could better prepare for downside risks. Under fiscal framework (balanced budget rule, debt issuance constraints), scope for countercyclical policy is limited. Recommendations: changing retail fuel price regime to create room for targeted support; implementing proposed reforms to fiscal framework (FEIP stabilization fund replenishment). Relevant to 5B.1 (fiscal agenda), 5B.9 (downside risk preparation), 5B.3 (fiscal framework credibility).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0026","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.1","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0025","unit-0027"],"explanation":"Medium-term fiscal strategy could help anchor expectations. Public debt ratio expected to remain broadly unchanged next decade. SRDSA indicates public debt remains sustainable. With proposed fiscal framework reform, credible debt anchor and medium-term strategy could increase fiscal policy flexibility as shock absorber. Reform elements: well-calibrated debt anchor, broader expenditure rule coverage, medium-term fiscal strategy with post-shock adjustment path, tighter escape clause triggers, strengthened fiscal council role. Pivotal for 5B.3 (fiscal rules credibility) and 5B.1 (medium-term fiscal position).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0027","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0026","unit-0028"],"explanation":"Authorities' Views on fuel price stabilization. Authorities prefer maintaining current retail fuel price stabilization mechanism given administration's pledge that fuel prices won't rise above November 2018 level. With oil prices expected to decline in 2023, formula should result in lower subsidies. Point to track record of tapering subsidies when market pressures abated. Interested in fiscal framework reforms to allocate fiscal savings to stabilization fund. Relevant to 5B.1 (fiscal priorities), 5B.9 (shock mitigation).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0028","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0027","unit-0029"],"explanation":"External Sector Policies. Peso faced less downward pressure than other EM currencies due to high interest rate differential vs U.S. Supported by strong remittances, fiscal discipline track record, nearshoring inflows. In event of weakening balance of payments, peso depreciation should act as shock absorber. FX markets deep and liquid. FX mismatches contained. Large shock might require policy rate hikes to counter inflation pass-through. Weak relevance to 5B.3 (exchange rate policy), 5B.9 (external shock management).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0029","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0028","unit-0030"],"explanation":"C. Maintaining a Robust Financial System. Financial system emerged from pandemic in good health. NPLs rose modestly from low levels then began declining. Capital adequacy ratios high and rising. Liquidity ratios comfortable. Banking system demonstrated strong resilience to severe macrofinancial shocks in solvency/liquidity stress tests under 2022 FSAP. Systemic vulnerabilities and liquidity risks broadly contained given high capital buffers, low private sector leverage, no stretched asset prices. Relevant to 5B.3 (financial system stability), 5B.5 (supervision).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0030","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0029","unit-0031"],"explanation":"Bank loans and financial health of non-financial corporations should be monitored given rapid rise in interest rates. Higher rates increase banks' net interest margin especially for larger institutions. With banks having increased holdings of domestic government bonds, could face mark-to-market losses (not expected to be large given short duration). Large fraction of NFC credit is floating rate - higher interest payments could strain liquidity and possibly increase defaults. NFCs retain relatively strong buffers; FSAP stress tests imply heightened default risks under adverse scenario would be manageable. Relevant to 5B.3 (financial sector), 5B.5 (corporate debt monitoring).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0031","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0030","unit-0032"],"explanation":"Authorities should take steps to enhance financial system resilience. Rolled out critical Basel reforms including TLAC requirements, improved supervisory techniques. 2022 FSAP recommendations: strengthen autonomy/resources of regulatory agencies, improve supervisory techniques (principles-based vs rules-based), enable consolidated supervision of financial conglomerates, enhance systemic liquidity management, strengthen safety nets, address cybersecurity, manage climate risks. Pivotal for 5B.3 (financial sector oversight) and 5B.5 (regulatory capacity).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0032","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.4","5B.3"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0031","unit-0033"],"explanation":"Macrofinancial toolkit could benefit from additional instruments. Mortgage market less well regulated - introducing LTV and DTI requirements now would be prudent ahead of possible risk buildup. Publishing macroprudential strategy and counter-cyclical buffer guidelines would advance macroprudential policy. Financial deepening should remain policy priority - difficulties in collateral recovery and judicial quality perceptions are headwinds. Weak relevance to 5B.4 (competition/financial development) and 5B.3 (macroprudential tools).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0033","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.4","5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0032","unit-0034"],"explanation":"Continue fostering Fintech development to increase competition and broaden financial inclusion. 2018 Fintech law was important step. Banxico launched plan for CBDC with primary objective of financial inclusion. AML/CFT framework aligned with FATF standards - focus should now be on effectiveness including beneficial ownership register, adequate resources, enforcement to ensure dissuasive sanctions. Emerging risks related to fintech and virtual assets need monitoring. Relevant to 5B.4 (competition), 5B.5 (financial integrity).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","source_sha256":"8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a","chunk_id":"unit-0034","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.10","5B.4","5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0033","unit-0035"],"explanation":"D. Policies for Higher and More Equitable Growth. Productivity growth has been weak despite successful trade opening and stable macro environment. NAFTA eliminated tariffs, reshaped economy with exports as share of GDP rising threefold. However, supply-side impediments held back productivity gains.
